notes: This contract pins the bounded timestamped Request Federation Save overload and the matching timestamped FederateAmbassador::initiateFederateSave(label, LogicalTime) callback to the exact IEEE 1516.1-2025 C++ declarations exported by the Requirements Lab. The dispatcher drains each recipient's in-process TSO payloads through the save timestamp, invokes Initiate Federate Save directly while the constrained recipient remains Time Advancing, and only then applies its grant; three-member TAR and TARA/NMRA Catch2 cases prove non-time-constrained notification is delayed until both constrained members have been admitted. A cross-member case proves one constrained member's queued TSO callback still precedes its own direct initiation after another member has entered the operation, and a request made during a recipient's in-transit callback proves direct initiation waits until delivery returns. The timestamped-save cases cover the inclusive TAR and NMR boundaries, the exclusive TARA and NMRA boundaries, and the strict actual Flush Queue Grant boundary: an FQR equal to the scheduled time leaves the request pending, while a later actual FQR grant admits it. Mixed FQR and ordinary constrained-member cases prequalify every member before the operation starts, and a six-member case exercises all five advance modes under the same save. Timed save/restore companions retain timestamp-eight default-source attribute and interaction passels across a timestamp-six boundary before restore and FQR delivery; RL-141 records the cross-service relation. The implementation remains an embedded development profile with in-memory save snapshots; durable persistence, general timed restore, protected review, package support, and conformance remain open.
